title: Transpose
description:
Write `Grid transpose(const Grid& grid)` that turns rows into columns: the element at `[r][c]` moves to `[c][r]`. A grid with 2 rows and 3 columns becomes one with 3 rows and 2 columns.

```
1 2 3          1 4
4 5 6    ->    2 5
               3 6
```

Every row of the input has the same length, and there is at least one row.
hints: Create the result with the right shape first: `Grid result(cols, std::vector<int>(rows));` (round brackets: "this many of these"). Then one nested loop copies each element to its mirrored position.
